chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Sukkari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Jawhari narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ammara narrated to us from his father. He said: al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him, said:
Whoever denies three things is not of our Shi'a: the Ascension (mi'raj), the questioning in the grave, and the intercession.

key_terms.الشَّفَاعَةُ: The intercession; the mediation of the Prophet and Imams on behalf of believers on Judgment Day
key_terms.الْمَسْأَلَةُ فِي الْقَبْرِ: The questioning in the grave; the interrogation by angels Munkar and Nakir after burial
key_terms.الْمِعْرَاجُ: The Ascension; the Prophet Muhammad's miraculous night journey through the heavens
key_terms.شِيعَتِنَا: Our Shi'a; the followers and partisans of the Ahlulbayt

ai.seo_question: What three beliefs must a Shi'a Muslim hold according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes three fundamental beliefs as prerequisites for being counted among the Shi'a: belief in the Prophet's miraculous night journey and ascension through the heavens (mi'raj), the interrogation of the deceased by angels Munkar and Nakir in the grave, and the intercession (shafa'a) of the Prophet and Imams on the Day of Judgment. These three doctrines represent core Shi'i creedal positions spanning the life of the Prophet, the intermediate realm after death, and the eschatological future.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan b. `Ali al-Sikri narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Zakariyya al-Jawhari narrated to us. He said: Ja`far b. Muhammad b. `Ammara narrated to us from his father.  He said: Al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as) said:
Whoever denies three things is not of our Shi`a: (1) the ascension (mi`raj), (2) the questioning in the grave, and (3) the intercession.
